record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: For every quasi-Banach operator ideal A and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals x(N0) and y(N0), determine whether there always exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) such that the reiteration identity (AAPP_x)APP_y = AAPP_z holds.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Show that, for every quasi-Banach operator ideal A and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals x(N0) and y(N0), there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) such that (AAPP_x)APP_y = AAPP_z.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{A}=(\mathcal{A},\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{A}})$ is, in the sense of Pietsch, a subclass of $\mathcal{L}$ equipped with a complete quasi-norm satisfying the usual ideal axioms (containment of finite-rank operators with $\|x\otimes y\|_{\mathcal{A}}=\|x\|\,\|y\|$, the two-sided ideal property $\|BTC\|_{\mathcal{A}}\le\|B\|\,\|T\|_{\mathcal{A}}\,\|C\|$, additivity up to a quasi-norm constant, and completeness of each component).

Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ be the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)\subseteq\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace, equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{x}$, that is solid (if $|s_n|\le|t_n|$ for all $n$ and $(t_n)\in x$ then $(s_n)\in x$ with $\|s\|_x\le\|t\|_x$). It is called shift-monotone if for the right-shift $S(s_0,s_1,s_2,\dots)=(0,s_0,s_1,\dots)$ one has $\|S s\|_x\le\|s\|_x$ for every $s\in x$.

For a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$, let $a_n(T;\mathcal{A})$ denote the $n$-th approximation number of $T$ relative to $\mathcal{A}$, defined by
$$a_n(T;\mathcal{A}):=\inf\{\|T-L\|_{\mathcal{A}} : L\in\mathcal{A},\ \mathrm{rank}(L)<n\},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$
Given a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the approximation procedure
$$\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x}:=\{T\in\mathcal{L} : (a_n(T;\mathcal{A}))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in x(\mathbb{N}_0)\},\qquad \|T\|_{\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x}}:= igl\|(a_n(T;\mathcal{A}))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0} igr\|_x.$$
This $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x}$ is again a quasi-Banach operator ideal.

Problem. Decide whether the following statement is true: for every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ and every pair $x(\mathbb{N}_0),\, y(\mathbb{N}_0)$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals, there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the reiteration identity
$$ igl(\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_x} igr)^{\mathrm{APP}_y}\;=\;\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{APP}_z}$$
holds as quasi-Banach operator ideals (with equivalent quasi-norms). If true, exhibit such a $z$ in terms of $x$ and $y$; if false, provide a counterexample.
